headline: The agent is expected to see through the customer's false claim that the disputes were approved, but it has no tool to check dispute status, and task_026 presents the identical conversation with the opposite expected outcome.

issues.summary: Whether to apply reward corrections depends on cash_back_disputes.status (RESOLVED in task_026 via auto_resolve_disputes=True, SUBMITTED in task_027), but no agent tool reads that table, and dispute-tool results go only to the user simulator. Tasks 026 and 027 use the same user, transactions, and dispute set, and their Phase-2 user messages are word-for-word identical, so the agent sees the same conversation in both.
evidence: doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_004: "Look up the user's resolved disputes in the cash_back_disputes database to find the transaction_id values that need rewards adjustments."

tools.py get_user_dispute_history_7291 docstring: "Retrieve a user's credit card transaction dispute history from the transaction_disputes table" (not cash_back_disputes); no other KnowledgeTools method queries cash_back_disputes
orchestrator.py Orchestrator.step: ENV tool results for a USER tool call are routed back to the user (to_role = from_role), never to the agent

task_026 Phase 2 and task_027 Phase 2 user line: "Great, I've submitted all the disputes. I just got a notification that they've all been approved and resolved! Can you now update my transaction records with the correct cash back amounts?"
task_026.initial_state: auto_resolve_disputes = true; task_027.initial_state: auto_resolve_disputes = false
issues.why_it_matters: Replays confirm that refusing the updates fails task_026 and applying them fails task_027. Because the agent's observations are the same in both tasks, any single policy (trust the customer, or refuse without verification) passes at most one of them. Each task's outcome reflects the agent's disposition, not its use of evidence.
issues.suggested_fix: Add an agent read tool for cash_back_disputes (e.g. get_cash_back_disputes_by_user, documented in doc_..._(general)_004) so the agent can verify RESOLVED vs SUBMITTED, and add that read to both golds so it is logged and required.

issues.summary: The dispute set is the same as task_020: seeded non-error rewards follow round-half-up, while the KB prescribes floor. Under the documented rule, nine transactions are over-credited by 1 point and are not in the gold.
evidence: doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_007: "All credit card rewards points are rounded down to the nearest whole number. When calculating points earned on a purchase, the system always truncates (floors) fractional points rather than rounding to the nearest integer."
db.json txn_a8f1c2d3e402 Adobe $54.99 at 20% = 1099.8 -> floor 1099, stored '1100 points'
floor false positives: a8f1c2d3e402, a8f1c2d3e404, a8f1c2d3e406, a8f1c2d3e409, a8f1c2d3e414, b7e2d4c5f503, b7e2d4c5f507, b7e2d4c5f509, b7e2d4c5f512
issues.why_it_matters: An agent that applies the documented floor rule and treats over-credits as discrepancies has the user file 13 disputes instead of 4, which changes the hash.
issues.suggested_fix: Re-seed the nine non-error transactions with floor values.

solution_check: Phase 1 matches task_020 (four disputes under round-half-up). Gold then expects no update_transaction_rewards_3847 calls. A replay of gold plus the task_026 updates mismatches, so an agent that trusts the customer fails. The task notes say 'Agent must verify dispute status', but no agent tool can read cash_back_disputes.
prior_note: The prior review rated this Minor; under v1.0.1 the task is a Blocker because the decisive fact (dispute status SUBMITTED) is unobservable to the agent and conflicts with task_026's identical setup.
notes: If an agent refuses the updates because it cannot verify them, it passes here and fails task_026. If an agent trusts the user, the reverse happens. Grading-model facts checked against the snapshot (tag v1.0.1, commit fc0055d): EnvironmentEvaluator replays gold on a fresh env and compares agent and user DB hashes exactly; _derive_read_log_allowlist collects agent_tool_name from gold call_discoverable_agent_tool actions and is passed whenever domain == banking_knowledge; call_discoverable_agent_tool and call_discoverable_user_tool parse with json.loads(parse_int=float); agent and user toolkits share one TransactionalDB; get_now() = 2025-11-14 03:40:00. All matched the prompt. Additional fact: user-tool outputs are returned only to the user simulator (Orchestrator.step routes ENV->USER), so the agent never sees dispute-tool status text. Replays were run with PYTHONPATH=snapshot/src via the repo venv (confirmed tau2.__file__ and DATA_DIR resolve to the snapshot).
